body: I have the similar requirement and I am facing the same issue as mentioned above. Is there a workaround?
Closing as a duplicate #2235. Also resolved in #2279
It looks like this is still happening intermittently in v0.71.0. Reopening

From Thiago:
> My 100% blind guess is we're creating a single file-like-object on upload and reusing it on every run — so if the file is closed and then gets reused it will brerak. To fix, we'd create a new file-like object each time.

Yup, the only thing is we aren't closing the file. My guess is the memory is being reclaimed and the file is getting closed for us. However, I was testing with a 189B file and though I wasn't able to repro consistently, I was able to do so and my machine should not be complaining about 189B. Definitely need to do more research to confirm. For sure we'll add better error handling, to recreate if possible but that to me is a bandaid. 

Additionally, re-creating a new file-like object each run when we have the file seems very suboptimal to me and a waste of memory...

issue.title: FileUploader: copy-on-write UploadedFile instances

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
Return a unique `UploadedFile` instance from every call to `st.file_uploader`. 

Closing or mutating an `UploadedFile` instance will not persist across multiple runs of a script. `UploadedFile` is copy-on-write and does not make a copy of the underlying bytes unless it's mutated.

- Instead of `UploadedFile`, the `UploadedFileManager` stores a new immutable `UploadedFileRec` internally
- `UploadedFileRec` just wraps a file's raw bytes and metadata
- `st.file_uploader` still returns `UploadedFile` instances, but they are now constructed on demand.
- `UploadedFile` has copy-on-write semantics - it does not copy its source data unless user code mutates the file. (This is the behavior of `BytesIO` when constructed with `bytes`: https://hg.python.org/cpython/rev/79a5fbe2c78f).

Fixes #2311

body:
I think this is the best thread to leave this -- I am encountering this error when using the `file_uploader` in combination with `st.radio()`, and `uploaded_file.seek(0)` does not solve the problem. Ill admit, I honestly do not understand what `seek(0)` is fundamentally doing, so maybe I am missing something obvious. Here is a minimal reproducible example:

```python3
import streamlit as st
import io

option = st.radio(
    'Choose method of submitting sequence:',
    ["Upload a file (.txt)", "Enter a sequence"])

txt = None

if option == "Upload a file (.txt)":

    uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a file:", type=['txt'])

    if uploaded_file is not None:
        uploaded_file.seek(0) #does not do anything
        text_io = io.TextIOWrapper(uploaded_file,encoding='UTF-8')
        txt=list(text_io.readlines())

elif option == "Enter a sequence":
    txt = st.text_area('Input sequence here:')

if txt:
    st.write(txt)
```
streamlit 0.71.0 and 0.72.0

When users upload a file, switch to manually entering text, and then try to upload again, the `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file` is thrown. This is a regression, as I did not encounter this error with a much older version of streamlit

any help would be much appreciated!

Thanks for sending this along. The fix was recently merged and will be available in version 0.73 that will be coming out this week. If you would like to get the latest, you can use our [`streamlit-nightly` package](https://pypi.org/project/streamlit-nightly/) that is updated with the latest changes every day.

issue.title: st.bokeh_chart double plot until browser resized

labels.name: type:regression
labels.description: This bug is a regression from previous behavior

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
Between versions 0.65 and 0.66 of Streamlit, running the following code snippet will cause a Bokeh plot to be duplicated:

https://gist.github.com/BitBernd/4cc06473d71de4a67ede607a618b0a83

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2762787/98823322-efb23b80-23ff-11eb-9a79-16226624604d.png)

To trigger the difference, running `pip install streamlit=0.65` to see the correct version, then `pip install streamlit==0.66` (or any version above that) to see the double-plotting. Move/resize the browser window slightly using 0.66+ and the duplicate plot will disappear. 

Ref: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/bokeh-produces-two-charts-when-deployed/5820/11
